conclusion: Adapt and rank can run concurrently after the same completed derive and immutable snapshot, within each existing two-core lane. No producer semantics need change. This is an implementation recommendation, not qualification or measured speedup.
dependency_evidence: common_input_batch.lane currently runs derive, snapshot, writes adapter_manifest, then adapt, rank, qualify. Rank argv references original raw source, selected-shards manifest and completed derived output/summary only; no adapted output is consumed.

adapt reads original raw/closed BT4 receipt data and derived replay/provenance read-only. It writes only adapted_output.writing, including ._raw_identity_cache, then atomically publishes adapted_output.
rank reads original raw and derived replay/provenance/eligibility read-only. It writes only rank_output.writing, including ._rank_identity_cache, then atomically publishes rank_output.

Both independently recheck source identities before publication. qualify requires both complete summaries, exact matching inventory/lineage, original snapshot stability and all-row ordinary consumer validation; leave this gate unchanged and start it only after both children succeed.
minimal_design: Keep derive and snapshot serial. Freeze/read summary and adapter manifest once, construct the same two argv arrays with unchanged values.

Extend only the existing stage start/poll/finalize mechanism to own a fixed pair of adapt and rank children. A single lane polling loop tracks both and calls the existing guard every polling interval; avoid a generic scheduler or concurrent calls sharing Guard state.

Keep separate GNU-time files/logs/started/completed receipts for each child and preserve every original command. Record actual overlap/start/end rather than summing overlapping wall times into elapsed duration.
Inherit existing lane timeout process group, affinity, CPUhidden environment, numeric-thread2 bootstrap, nice19 and ionice3. Do not create detached stage sessions that escape the lane timeout.

On spawn/started-receipt/child/resource/STOP failure, cancel and reap both owned children, propagate failure promptly so existing parent whole-lane process-group cleanup kills descendants, preserve partial/final sibling evidence, and never enter qualify or emit lane/package completion. Independent timeout still bounds children after coordinator death.
Wait for both zero exits and valid timing receipts, then unchanged qualify, final pin/storage/guard checks and completion. No retries/adoption/changes to current frozen runtime.

Make concurrency explicit in the future frozen plan/receipt; preserve serial default for old manifests if adding an option. A single opt-in adapter_rank_overlap boolean is sufficient, not a general stage DAG.
resources_and_interpretation: Historical adapt and rank CPU time approximately equals their wall time; derive consumes approximately two CPUs. Two overlapping readers may use the lane two-core allocation more fully without expanding its cpuset.

Both processes retain two numerical/compression threads, so bursts can contend within the same two-core cpuset. Do not silently change thread settings while attributing any benefit solely to stage overlap.

Run06 ideal critical path saves679.01 seconds (~25.10% of summed stage wall); run07 saves673.85 seconds. Actual simultaneous raw decompression, Zarr reads, hashing, page cache and disk writes may reduce or reverse this saving. This is no measured25% throughput claim.

The actual manifest8GiB limit is new_output_cache_bytes, sampled every60s; it is not a process RAM cap. Two cache budgets64MiB each can coexist per lane. Keep the same aggregate cache/output and150GiB free-space guards; concurrency does not make sampled bounds instantaneous.

Summed separately measured adapt+rank peak RSS is about2.00GiB per lane and3.99GiB over both lanes. This is a conservative historical addition, not a measured simultaneous peak or hard bound; account for lane/owner imports and other active jobs.

Current output totals fit previous allowance, but overlapping private cache lifetimes add potential128MiB across two lanes versus serialized cache residency. Reuse existing guard rather than increase budget invisibly.
meaningful_future_tests: Actual tiny pair barrier proves both children are live concurrently under the lane cpuset and qualify begins only after both complete; compare semantic payload arrays/provenance/inventory with serial baseline, allowing timestamps/paths/receipts to differ.
One child fails while sibling owns a sleeping grandchild: assert whole owned group is eventually absent/zombie within bounded wait, unrelated sentinel survives, qualify and lane completion absent.
Second spawn or started-receipt write failure after first child begins cleans first child/descendants; preserve partial evidence.

STOP/deadline/output-bound event while both run exercises same fail-cleanup path. Existing tests cover two independent source lanes and serial stages, but do not establish this new within-lane fan-out.
limits: No edits, tests, corpus payload reads, new timing, GPU, process changes or operational launch. Actual future implementation, resource window and immutable runtime binding require separate review.
